Acquisition: channels, leads and neutral offers

After this lesson you can:
  • List the acquisition channels an RE typically runs and their governance differences
  • Explain lead attribution and why duplicate/existing-customer matching matters
  • State the neutrality rules for multi-lender offer presentation

Learning rhythm: read one section at a time, pause to explain the control in your own words, then answer the knowledge check without looking back.

On this page
  1. Where applications come from
  2. Leads are governed objects too
  3. Presenting offers without tricks
  4. Regulatory anchors
  5. Where this lives in LoanOS
  6. Knowledge check

1. Where applications come from

An RE's pipeline blends channels with very different risk profiles:

  • Digital self-serve — the borrower applies on the RE's own DLA.
  • Branch-assisted — staff capture the application with the borrower present.
  • Partner-sourced — DSAs, business correspondents, dealers, merchants and LSPs bring leads.
  • API / embedded finance — a partner platform originates inside its own journey.

Each channel carries its own conduct duties: partner channels need commission governance and conduct monitoring; digital channels need consent and disclosure evidence; every channel needs source attribution so the RE can answer 'who brought this borrower and what were they promised?'

2. Leads are governed objects too

Before an application exists there is a lead: a source, a campaign, a referral, an attribution trail, and a follow-up history. Two controls matter early:

  1. Duplicate and existing-customer matching — the same person applying twice through two DSAs must converge on one customer record, or exposure and KYC fragment.
  2. Channel eligibility and serviceability — geography, product entitlement and branch routing decide whether the RE may even serve the lead.

A BA writing acquisition requirements should treat abandonment, re-application and channel switching as first-class paths, not exceptions.

3. Presenting offers without tricks

When a surface presents offers from multiple lenders, the Digital Lending Directions and consumer-protection rules require neutrality: complete offers (all-in cost, not teaser rates), objective and disclosed ranking, unmatched lenders visible where required, and no dark patterns — no pre-ticked add-ons, no buried fees, no countdown pressure. LoanOS encodes ranking disclosure and dark-pattern prevention as offer-surface capabilities rather than leaving it to marketing judgement.

Regulatory anchors

  • RBI-DL-2025 — Channel sourcing never transfers lender responsibility; partner conduct stays visible and auditable to the RE.
  • CCPA-DARK-PATTERNS — Offer comparison must avoid deceptive patterns; ranking must be explained.

Family IDs resolve in the India regulatory register (docs/compliance/india-regulatory-register.md), which owns sources and caveats.

Where this lives in LoanOS

  • Capability CHN-003 — DSA, BC, connector, dealer, merchant and LSP lead intake.
  • Capability CHN-007 — Duplicate-lead and existing-customer matching.
  • Capability OFR-002 — Multi-lender matching and complete offer presentation.
  • App surface /t/{tenantId}/portal/ — Borrower-facing journey portal — the RE-owned digital channel (tenant-scoped).

Knowledge check

Answer aloud or write your choice before opening the explanation. If you miss it, revisit the named section—not the whole lesson.

1. Why must duplicate leads converge on one customer record?

  1. To save storage
  2. So exposure, KYC and conduct history aggregate on one person
  3. To pay only one DSA
  4. RBI mandates one lead per person
Reveal answer and reasoning

B. Fragmented identity breaks exposure aggregation, KYC reuse and conduct attribution — all of which regulation expects at the customer level.
